column1: KAP23 Sec 2.4 L1.2: 'using oversampling before splitting the data into training and test sets leads to an imperfect separation'; Table 1 cites Blagus and Lusa 2015 (bioinformatics, 6 papers).
column2: KAP23 Sec 2.4 L1.2 (verified in full text): \qFor instance, using oversampling before splitting the data into training and test sets leads to an imperfect separation between the training and test sets since data generated using oversampling from the training set will also be present in the test set.\q Table 1 lists Blagus and Lusa 2015 (bioinformatics, 6 papers).

column1: KAP23 Sec 2.4 L1.2: 'Using the entire dataset for any pre-processing steps such as imputation or over/under sampling'; Appendix B.4 (Wang 2019): 17.4% of values missing; imputing training and test separately within each fold dramatically reduces performance.
column2: KAP23 Sec 2.4 L1.2 (verified): \qUsing the entire dataset for any pre-processing steps such as imputation or over/under sampling.\q Appendix B.4: \qCorrecting the imputation method dramatically reduces the performance of the ML models proposed.\q

column1: KAP23 Sec 2.4 L1.4: 'If a dataset with duplicates is used for the purposes of training and evaluating an ML model, the same data could exist in the training as well as test set.'
column2: KAP23 Sec 2.4 L1.4 (verified): \qIf a dataset with duplicates is used for the purposes of training and evaluating an ML model, the same data could exist in the training as well as test set.\q

column2: KAP23 Sec 2.4 L1.2 (verified): \qusing oversampling before splitting the data into training and test sets leads to an imperfect separation between the training and test sets\q; L1.4: \qthe same data could exist in the training as well as test set.\q Prereg tie rule: oversampling by copying rows is L1.4.

column1: KAP23 Sec 2.4 L3.1 and Appendix B.5 (Kaufman et al. 2019): k-fold cross validation shuffles, so 'the training dataset could contain data from a later date than the test dataset'.
column2: KAP23 Appendix B.5 (verified): \qWhen the dataset contains temporal data, the training dataset could contain data from a later date than the test dataset because of being shuffled.\q

column1: KAP23 Sec 2.4 L3.1: 'If the test set contains data from before the training set, the model is built using data from the future that it should not have access to'.
column2: KAP23 Sec 2.4 L3.1 (verified): \qIf the test set contains data from before the training set, the model is built using data from the future that it should not have access to during training, and can cause leakage.\q

column1: KAP23 Sec 2.4 L3.2: Oner et al. 2020 find a histopathology study 'uses different observations of the same patient in the training and test sets'; the claim is about new patients.
column2: KAP23 Sec 2.4 L3.2 (verified): \qOner et al. 2020 find that a recent study on histopathology uses different observations of the same patient in the training and test sets.\q (The claim is about new patients.)

column1: KAP23 Sec 2.4 L3.2: 'train and test samples come from the same people or units'; block cross validation (Roberts 2017, Valavi 2021) as remedy.
column2: KAP23 Sec 2.4 L3.2 (verified): \qIn the extreme (but unfortunately common) case, train and test samples come from the same people or units.\q Remedy named there: block cross validation (Roberts 2017, Valavi 2021).
